summary: Concrete cast against rough timber boards, so each board's grain and joint is printed in its face.
_comment: Board-formed concrete: cast-in-place concrete poured against rough-sawn timber boards, so the face keeps each board's imprint: vertical strips 8 to 12 cm wide, each a slightly different plane and tone, the sawn grain printed into each, thin paste fins at the joints, the odd knot, bug holes and two form-tie holes. The maps are generated (L2, gen_concrete_boardformed.py); the mean colour and roughness are anchored to Physically Based 'Concrete'. Re-made at its tag (2026-10-31, Phase19 D-9): it was the ambientCG Concrete045 scan at 200 cm, off its s1 tag, and that scan is a 0.67 m sample repeated three times down the tile, so no exact 1 m tile could be cut or quilted from it without breaking its boards. The tile is exactly 1 m at about 1 mm a texel; the boards' widths sum to it, so it wraps on a joint, and the boards run through it with no butt joint. It is one substance carrying an imprint, not an assembly (D1). Opaque: a matte, porous solid. Carries every relevant wear layer at 0 (C1): cracks (overlay 1, damage; Cracks01 draws a crazing network, the right shape for concrete), scratches, dust as a deposit (Phase10), gated by the Grime mask. Not carried: the wet look and efflorescence the wish list also wants. Built by the Phase11 batch.
name: Concrete_BoardFormed_Clean_Base_s1_v01

sources.note: base_color_const is the generated basecolor's MEAN and roughness_const the roughness map's mean (both re-anchored exactly); specular_ior and metalness are taken as given.

sources.why: board widths 8 to 12 cm, fins, knots, bug holes and tie holes sized from board-formed walls; no measured value. meters_per_tile 1.0 is the s1 scale option's length; the generator makes the tile at that size (a texel of about 1 mm), its features sized in metres, never stretched.
